- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce overshoot by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid underestimating — add 3–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- If recent price spike (last 3–5 days) is followed by forecast overreaction, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–5% from forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive >0.5), adjust downward by 1–3% to account for overconfidence.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), reduce forecast variance — use 20% smoothing of previous 7-day average.  
- For high volatility periods (e.g., >10% price swings in last 5 days), apply lag correction: forecast 30d should be 1–2 days behind actual trend.
